question: Does a stationary run stop too early under under-relaxation in every SWAN version, or only in the fork?
deck: examples/nonlinear_interactions/quad/quad_dia2.swn: a 1D fetch case, 41 grid points, default numerics with NUMERIC STOPC STAT MXITST=500 and the ALFA below, so that the iteration limit never applies.

programs.rws4131: RWS 41.31A.1, the Rijkswaterstaat production build of 41.31 (Intel), run with one OpenMP thread

finding: Every run reports 'accuracy OK in 100.00 %'. Under-relaxation changes the path of the iteration, not its end point, so every column should be equal; instead Hs falls as ALFA rises, in all three programs. At ALFA=0.01, Hs at 25 km is 26% below the run without under-relaxation for the fork and for upstream, and 25% below for RWS 41.31A.1. The mechanism has been in SWAN since at least 41.31.
note: The fork and upstream differ at ALFA=0.05 (11 against 2 iterations) because upstream reads an unset KTETA in decks without breaking (BF-16); the fork sets it. Each program is compared only with itself.
